title: Analytic strict derivatives, local homeomorphisms and analytic inverses
statement: Let $E,F$ be finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] normed complex vector spaces and $f:E\to F$. Analytic at $a$ means represented near $a$ by a convergent complex power series. A strict derivative $L$ at $a$ means $\|f(x)-f(y)-L(x-y)\|=o(\|x-y\|)$ as $(x,y)\to(a,a)$. An open partial homeomorphism $e:E\dashrightarrow F$ consists of open source and target subsets, mutually inverse continuous maps between them, and arbitrary extensions of these maps off those subsets. The following hold. (1) If $f$ is analytic at $a$, it has strict derivative $Df(a)$ at $a$. (2) If $f$ has strict derivative $i$ at $a$, where $i:E\simeq_{\mathbf C}F$ is a continuous linear equivalence, there is an open partial homeomorphism $e$ whose forward function is $f$ and whose source contains $a$. (3) For any open partial homeomorphism $e$ and $a$ in its source, if its forward function is analytic at $a$ and $De(a)=i$ for a continuous complex-linear equivalence $i$, then its inverse function is analytic at $e(a)$. (4) A map $f:E\to F$ analytic at $a$ is analytic at every point of some open ball of positive radius centred at $a$.
